title: India Most Represented in THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027; Saveetha Retains Top Spot in India
summary: With 102 universities, India is the most represented country in the THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027, and Saveetha, Chennai, remains India's top institution at 62nd.
body_html:
Chennai, 19 November 2026: India has become the most represented country in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027, with 102 Indian universities among 1,058 institutions from 102 countries and territories. Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences (SIMATS), Chennai, has retained its place as India’s highest-ranked institution in the ranking, at 62nd globally.

Indian participation in the ranking has grown steadily over its three editions, from 65 universities in 2025 to 88 in 2026 and 102 in 2027, an increase of nearly 57% in two years. Indian institutions now make up approximately 9.6% of the universities ranked. The release notes that this reflects a widening base of institutions taking part in interdisciplinary science, although representation alone is not a measure of research quality.

Seven Indian universities feature in the global top 100. Saveetha recorded an overall score of 66.9, followed by Jamia Millia Islamia (69th globally; 65.6), Lovely Professional University (80th; 63.6), SRM Institute of Science and Technology (82nd; 63.3), Amity University, Noida (85th; 63.2), Manipal Academy of Higher Education (87th; 62.9) and Anna University (100th; 61.9).

Saveetha’s Research Outputs score of 75.5 was the highest among these seven institutions, ahead of Lovely Professional University (71.3), SRM (67.2), Jamia Millia Islamia (66.5), Manipal (62.1), Amity (62.0) and Anna University (60.7). Its Research Inputs and Research Process scores were 65.5 and 33.3 respectively. The Outputs dimension carries the largest weight in THE’s methodology.

The institution has moved up from 102nd globally in the inaugural 2025 edition to 57th in 2026, when it first became India’s top-ranked institution. In the 2027 edition it is placed 62nd, 40 positions higher than in the first edition despite a five-place movement from last year.

Saveetha brings together medicine, dentistry, engineering, pharmacy, nursing, allied health sciences and other disciplines, with collaboration among clinicians, engineers and scientists in areas such as medical technology, biotechnology, artificial intelligence and digital healthcare.

According to the release, India’s broad participation across central, state, private and deemed-to-be universities shows the growing reach of interdisciplinary research in the country, and the next challenge is to turn this participation into stronger research impact and greater representation in the highest tiers of the ranking. The THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027 are published in association with Schmidt Science Fellows.
